paragraphs: We are a worldwide franchisor, operator, and licensor of hotel, residential, timeshare, and other lodging properties under a portfolio of compelling brands at different price and service points. Consistent with our focus on franchising, management, and licensing, we own or lease very few of our lodging properties (less than one percent of our system). As of year-end 2025, our system included 9,805 properties (1,779,936 rooms) in 145 countries and territories, and we also had approximately 4,100 properties (nearly 610,000 rooms) in our development pipeline.

We discuss our operations in the following reportable business segments: (1) U.S. & Canada, (2) Europe, Middle East & Africa ("EMEA"), (3) Greater China, and (4) Asia Pacific excluding China ("APEC"). Our Caribbean & Latin America ("CALA") operating segment does not meet the applicable accounting criteria for separate disclosure as a reportable business segment, and as such, we include its results in "Unallocated corporate and other." See Note 14 for more information.

We believe that our brand portfolio offers the most compelling range of brands, lodging properties, and other offerings in hospitality. Our brands are categorized by style of offering - Classic and Distinctive. Our Classic brands offer time-honored hospitality for the modern traveler, and our Distinctive brands offer memorable experiences with a unique perspective - each of which we group into four quality tiers: Luxury, Premium, Select, and Midscale. Luxury offers bespoke and superb amenities and services. Premium offers sophisticated and thoughtful amenities and services. Select offers smart and easy amenities and services. Midscale offers limited services and essential amenities at a more affordable price point. Longer stay brands, which are classified under multiple quality tiers, offer amenities suggestive of the comforts of home. We are subject to various risks that make an investment in our securities risky. The events and consequences discussed in these risk factors could, in circumstances we may or may not be able to accurately predict, recognize, or control, have a material adverse effect on our business, liquidity, financial condition, and results of operations. In addition, these risks could cause

results to differ materially from those we express in forward-looking statements contained in this report or in other Company communications. These risk factors do not identify all risks that we face, and our business could also be affected by factors, events, or uncertainties that are not presently known to us or that we currently do not consider to present significant risks to our operations.

Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully for guests. We operate in markets that contain many competitors. Our hotel brands and other lodging offerings generally compete with regional, national, and international chains that operate lodging properties or franchise their brands, lodging properties that are not affiliated with a chain, and online platforms that allow travelers to book short-term rentals of homes and apartments. Our ability to remain competitive and attract and retain business, group, and leisure travelers depends on our success in distinguishing and driving preference for our lodging products and services, including our Loyalty Program, direct digital channels, consumer-facing technology platforms and services, our co-branded credit cards, and other offerings. If we cannot compete successfully in these areas, our business, liquidity, financial condition, and results of operations could be materially adversely affected. Further, new lodging supply in individual markets could have a negative impact on the hotel industry and hamper our ability to maintain or increase room rates or occupancy in those markets.

Economic and other global, national, and regional conditions and events have in the past materially impacted, and could in the future materially impact, our business, operations, financial results, and growth. Because we conduct our business on a global scale, we are affected by changes and uncertainties in global, national, or regional economies, governmental policies (including in areas such as trade, travel, spending, immigration, labor, healthcare, and related issues), and geopolitical, public health, social and other conditions and events. Our business, financial results, and growth are impacted by weak or volatile economic conditions; pandemics and other outbreaks of disease; natural and man-made disasters; changes in energy prices, interest rates, inflation, and currency values; political instability, geopolitical disputes or conflict, actual or threatened war, terrorist activity, civil unrest and other acts of violence; heightened travel security measures, travel advisories, and disruptions in air and ground travel; and concerns over the foregoing. These conditions and events have in the past materially negatively impacted, and could in the future materially negatively impact, our business, operations, financial results, and growth in many ways, including, but not limited to, as follows:
•reducing revenues at hotels in our system, impacting our fees and the ability of hotels to meet expenses, including payment of amounts owed to us;
•reducing revenues we receive from other programs and offerings; •adversely affecting the value of our owned and leased properties or investments;

We are a worldwide franchisor, operator, and licensor of hotel, residential, timeshare, and other lodging properties under a portfolio of compelling brands at different price and service points. We discuss our operations in the following reportable business segments: (1) U.S. & Canada, (2) Europe, Middle East & Africa ("EMEA"), (3) Greater China, and (4) Asia Pacific excluding China ("APEC"). Our Caribbean & Latin America ("CALA") operating segment does not meet the applicable accounting criteria for separate disclosure as a reportable business segment, and as such, we include its results in "Unallocated corporate and other."

Under our asset-light business model and consistent with our focus on franchising, management, and licensing, we own or lease very few of our lodging properties. Under our hotel franchising arrangements, we generally receive an initial application fee and continuing royalty fees, which are typically based on a percentage of room revenues, plus for certain brands, a percentage of food and beverage revenues. Terms of our management agreements vary, but we earn a management fee that is typically composed of a base management fee, which is a percentage of the revenues of the hotel, and an incentive management fee, which is based on the profits of the hotel. In many cases (particularly in our U.S. & Canada, Europe, and CALA regions), incentive management fees are subject to a specified owner return. We also have license and other agreements with third parties for certain offerings, such as for our timeshare properties, MGM Collection with Marriott Bonvoy, Design Hotels, and The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, under which we receive royalty and certain other fees. Additionally, we earn fees for other uses of our intellectual property, including primarily co-branded credit card fees, as well as residential branding fees and certain other licensing fees.

We believe Revenue per Available Room ("RevPAR"), which we calculate by dividing property level room revenue by total rooms available for the period, is a meaningful indicator of our performance because it measures the period-over-period change in room revenues. RevPAR may not be comparable to similarly titled measures, such as revenues, and should not be viewed as necessarily correlating with our fee revenue. We also believe occupancy and average daily rate ("ADR"), which are components of calculating RevPAR, are meaningful indicators of our performance. Occupancy, which we calculate by dividing total rooms sold by total rooms available for the period, measures the utilization of a property's available capacity. ADR, which we calculate by dividing property level room revenue by total rooms sold, measures average room price and is useful in assessing pricing levels. Unless otherwise stated, RevPAR, occupancy, and ADR statistics are on a systemwide basis for comparable properties, and all changes refer to year-over-year changes for the comparable period. Comparisons to prior periods are on a constant U.S. dollar basis, which we calculate by applying exchange rates for the current period to the prior comparable period. We believe constant dollar analysis provides valuable information regarding the performance of hotels in our system as it removes currency fluctuations from the presentation of such results.

We define our comparable properties as hotels in our system that were open and operating under one of our brands since the beginning of the last full calendar year (since January 1, 2024 for the current period) and have not, in either the current or previous year: (1) undergone significant room or public space renovations or expansions, (2) been converted between company-operated and franchised, or (3) sustained substantial property damage or business interruption. Our comparable properties also exclude MGM Collection with Marriott Bonvoy, Design Hotels, The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, residences, and timeshare properties. For 2025, we had 5,554 comparable U.S. & Canada properties and 2,011 comparable International properties.
In 2025, worldwide RevPAR increased 2.0 percent compared to 2024, driven by ADR growth of 2.1 percent.

In the U.S. & Canada, RevPAR increased 0.7 percent in 2025, reflecting strong demand at our luxury hotels, partially offset by softer demand at our select service hotels, which were impacted by weaker business transient demand, in part due to declines in government travel.

In our International regions, RevPAR increased 5.1 percent in 2025, reflecting higher demand in most countries across the APEC, EMEA, and CALA regions. In Greater China, RevPAR increased 0.4 percent, reflecting softness in macro-economic conditions during the year.

On November 30, 2018, we announced a data security incident involving unauthorized access to the Starwood reservations database (the "Data Security Incident"). We are currently unable to reasonably estimate the range of total possible financial impact to the Company from the Data Security Incident in excess of the expenses already recorded; however, we do not believe this incident will impact our long-term financial health. See Note 7 for additional information related to legal proceedings, investigations, and insurance recoveries related to the Data Security Incident.

Our system grew from 9,361 properties (1,706,331 rooms) at year-end 2024 to 9,805 properties (1,779,936 rooms) at year-end 2025. The increase compared to year-end 2024 reflected gross additions of 703 properties (99,459 rooms), including the addition of 37 properties (8,789 rooms) from the citizenM brand acquisition discussed in Note 3, and deletions of 253 properties (25,643 rooms). The property and room counts as of year-end 2025 reflect the removal of all Sonder properties from our portfolio. Our 2025 gross room additions included nearly 64,000 rooms located outside U.S. & Canada (including the citizenM brand acquisition) and roughly 33,400 rooms converted from competitor brands.

At year-end 2025, we had approximately 4,100 properties and nearly 610,000 rooms in our development pipeline, which included over 35,000 rooms approved for development but not yet under signed contracts. At year-end 2025, our development pipeline included nearly 265,000 rooms, or 43 percent, that were under construction, including hotels that are in the process of converting to our system. Over half of the rooms in our development pipeline were located outside U.S. & Canada.

In 2025, we signed nearly 1,200 development deals with hotel owners and other counterparties (excluding the citizenM acquisition) representing approximately 163,000 rooms globally. Over 30 percent of rooms signed were driven by conversion opportunities. During 2025, we added three new brands to our portfolio through the citizenM brand acquisition and the introductions of Series by Marriott and the Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy. We continued to expand our portfolio across chain scales, including advancing the expansion of our midscale offerings, and we also continued to strengthen our residential portfolio, signing 55 residential agreements in 2025.
In 2026, we expect net rooms growth of 4.5 to 5.0 percent.

paragraphs: 我們是一家全球性的特許經營商、營運商及授權商，經營旅館、住宅、時租屋及其他住宿設施，旗下擁有不同價格與服務層次的強大品牌組合。與我們專注於特許經營、管理及授權的策略一致，我們擁有或租賃的住宿設施非常有限（少於我們系統總數的百分之一）。截至2025年底，我們的系統包含145個國家及地區的9,805處設施（1,779,936間客房），並擁有約4,100處設施（近610,000間客房）在開發管道中。
我們在以下應報告分部中說明我們的營運情況：(1) 美國與加拿大、(2) 歐洲、中東與非洲（"EMEA"）、(3) 大中華區，以及(4) 亞太地區 excluding 中國（"APEC"）。我們的加勒比海與拉丁美洲（"CALA"）營運分部未符合適用的會計準則，因此不作為應報告分部進行獨立披露，因此我們將其結果歸入 "未分配的企業及其它"。請參閱附註14以取得更多資訊。

我們認為，我們的品牌組合提供了最具吸引力的品牌、住宿設施及其他服務。我們的品牌根據服務風格分為經典與特色兩類。經典品牌提供歷久彌新的住宿體驗，而特色品牌則提供難忘的體驗與獨特的視角，我們將其歸納為四種品質層級：豪華、高檔、精選與中階。豪華品牌提供訂製化與卓越的設施與服務。高檔品牌提供精緻且貼心的設施與服務。精選品牌提供智慧且簡便的設施與服務。中階品牌則提供有限的服務與基本設施，價格更具競爭力。長期住宿品牌，根據多種品質層級分類，提供類似家的舒適設施。下述表格顯示Marriott於2025年底開放的旗下品牌組合。

本公司為全球性酒店、住宅、時租旅館及其他住宿設施的特許經營商、營運商及授權商，旗下擁有不同價格與服務層次的強勢品牌組合。我們的營運業務分為以下應報告分部：(1) 美國與加拿大，(2) 歐洲、中東與非洲（"EMEA"），(3) 大中華區，(4) 亞太地區（不包括中國）（"APEC"）。我們的加勒比海與拉丁美洲（"CALA"）營運分部未符合適用會計準則中應獨立披露為應報告業務分部的條件，因此我們將其結果歸入"未分配之公司及其它"項目中。

根據我們的輕資產營運模式，並配合我們對特許經營、管理及授權的重視，我們擁有或租賃的住宿設施極少。根據我們的酒店特許經營協議，我們通常會收取初始申請費及持續性 royalty 費，這些費用通常以房間營收的百分比計算，部分品牌則另外計入餐飲營收的百分比。我們的管理協議條款各有不同，但我們通常會收取管理費，該費用通常由基本管理費（以酒店營收的百分比計算）及激勵管理費（以酒店利潤的百分比計算）組成。在許多情況下（特別是在美國與加拿大、歐洲及 CALA 區域），激勵管理費會受到指定業主回報的限制。我們也與第三方簽訂授權及其他協議，例如時租旅館、MGM Collection with Marriott Bonvoy、Design Hotels 及 The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection，根據這些協議，我們會收取 royalty 及其他費用。此外，我們也會因智慧財產權的其他使用而獲得費用，包括主要為共用信用卡費用、住宅品牌費用及某些其他授權費用。

我們認為每間可用房間收入（"RevPAR"），我們以將房間營收除以該期間總可用房間數計算，是衡量我們表現的重要指標，因為它反映了房間營收的期間變化。RevPAR 可能與同名稱的其他指標（如營收）不具可比性，也不應視為與我們的費用收入必然相關。我們也認為入住率及平均房價（"ADR"），這些為計算 RevPAR 的組成部分，是衡量我們表現的重要指標。入住率，我們以將銷售房間數除以該期間總可用房間數計算，用以衡量住宿設施可用容量的使用情況。ADR，我們以將房間營收除以銷售房間數計算，用以衡量平均房間價格，並有助於評估價格水準。除非另有說明，RevPAR、入住率及 ADR 統計數據均以可比住宿設施為基礎，所有變動均指與去年同期的變動。與前一時期的比較均以美國幣幣值為基礎，我們以當前期間的匯率套用至前一可比期間的數據計算。我們認為常態幣分析能提供有關我們系統內酒店表現的重要資訊，因為它剔除了貨幣波動對這些結果呈現的影響。

我們將可比住宿設施定義為在系統內、自上一個完整會計年度開始（即自2024年1月1日起）以來一直營運且屬於我們品牌之一的酒店，且在當前或前一年度未經歷以下情況：(1) 進行重大房間或公共空間翻修或擴建，(2) 從公司營運轉為特許經營或反之，或(3) 遭受重大財產損壞或業務中斷。我們的可比住宿設施也排除 MGM Collection with Marriott Bonvoy、Design Hotels、The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection、住宅及時租旅館。2025年，我們有5,554間可比的美國與加拿大住宿設施及2,011間可比的國際住宿設施。
2025年，全球 RevPAR 增加2.0%，主要因 ADR 增長2.1%。
在美國與加拿大，2025年 RevPAR 增加0.7%，反映我們豪華酒店需求強勁，部分抵銷了我們選擇服務酒店需求較弱的影響，後者因商業旅客需求較弱，部分歸因於政府旅遊減少。
在國際區域，2025年 RevPAR 增加5.1%，反映 APEC、EMEA 及 CALA 區域大多數國家需求上升。在大中華區，RevPAR 增加0.4%，反映該年度總體經濟條件較弱。
2018年11月30日，我們宣佈發生一起資料安全事件，涉及未經授權存取Starwood預訂資料庫（"資料安全事件"）。目前我們無法合理估計此資料安全事件對本公司可能造成的總體財務影響，且此影響超過已記入費用的部分；然而，我們不認為此事件會影響我們的長期財務狀況。有關資料安全事件相關法律程序、調查及保險賠償的更多資訊，請參閱附註7。

我們的系統在2024年底為9,361間飯店（1,706,331間客房），至2025年底成長為9,805間飯店（1,779,936間客房）。與2024年底相比，成長反映總計增加703間飯店（99,459間客房），包括透過附註3所述的citizenM品牌收購新增的37間飯店（8,789間客房），以及減少253間飯店（25,643間客房）。2025年底的飯店與客房數量反映已移除所有Sonder飯店。我們2025年的總計客房增加包含近64,000間位於美國與加拿大以外的客房（包括citizenM品牌收購），以及約33,400間由競爭對手品牌轉換而來的客房。
2025年底，我們的開發管道中約有4,100間飯店與近610,000間客房，其中包括已批准開發但尚未簽訂合約的超過35,000間客房。2025年底，我們的開發管道中約有265,000間客房，或佔43％，正在建設中，包括正在轉換至我們系統的飯店。我們開發管道中超過一半的客房位於美國與加拿大以外。

2025年，我們與飯店業主及其他對手簽訂了近1,200筆開發協議，代表全球約163,000間客房（不包括citizenM收購）。超過30％的簽訂客房是由轉換機會所驅動。在2025年，我們透過citizenM品牌收購以及Series by Marriott與Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy的引入，將三個新品牌加入我們的產品組合。我們持續擴展產品組合的規模，包括推進中端產品的擴張，同時也持續強化住宅產品組合，2025年我們簽訂了55筆住宅協議。
2026年，我們預期淨客房成長為4.5至5.0％。

paragraphs: 本公司面臨多種風險，使投資本公司證券變得風險較高。這些風險因素所討論的事件及其後果，可能在某些我們可能無法準確預測、認知或控制的情況下，對本公司業務、流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。此外，這些風險可能會導致結果與本公司在本報告或其他本公司通訊中所表達的預測性陳述有重大差異。這些風險因素並未識別本公司所面臨的所有風險，且本公司業務也可能受到目前未知或本公司目前認為對營運並無重大風險的其他因素、事件或不確定性影響。

本公司所屬產業競爭激烈，這可能會影響本公司成功爭取旅客的能力。本公司營運的市場包含許多競爭對手。本公司酒店品牌及其他住宿服務通常與區域性、國家性及國際性連鎖企業競爭，這些企業經營住宿設施或特許經營其品牌，以及非連鎖企業經營的住宿設施，以及允許旅客預訂短期住宅及公寓的線上平台。本公司能否在這些領域保持競爭力並吸引及留住商務、團體及休閒旅客，取決於本公司成功區分並推動偏好本公司住宿產品與服務的能力，包括本公司忠誠計畫、直接數位通路、面對消費者科技平台與服務、本公司合作信用卡及其它服務。若本公司無法在這些領域成功競爭，則本公司業務、流動性、財務狀況及營運成果可能受到重大不利影響。此外，個別市場的新住宿供給可能會對酒店產業產生負面影響，並阻礙本公司維持或提高這些市場的房間價格或入住率的能力。

經濟及其他全球、國家及區域的情況與事件，過去已對本公司業務、營運、財務結果及成長產生重大影響，未來也可能對本公司業務、營運、財務結果及成長產生重大影響。因為本公司業務在全球範圍內進行，因此受到全球、國家或區域經濟變化與不確定性、政府政策（包括貿易、旅遊、支出、移民、勞動、醫療及相關議題）以及地緣政治、公共衛生、社會及其他情況與事件的影響。本公司業務、財務結果及成長受到經濟弱勢或波動的影響；疫情及其他疾病爆發；自然與人為災難；能源價格、利率、通貨膨脹及貨幣價值的變化；政治不穩定、地緣政治爭議或衝突、實際或威脅的戰爭、恐怖活動、民變及其他暴力行為；提高的旅遊安全措施、旅遊建議及航空與地面交通的中斷；以及對上述情況的擔憂。這些情況與事件過去已對本公司業務、營運、財務結果及成長產生重大負面影響，未來也可能對本公司業務、營運、財務結果及成長產生重大負面影響，包括但不限於以下方式：
•減少本公司系統內酒店的收入，影響本公司費用及酒店支付應付本公司金額的能力；
•減少本公司從其他計畫與服務所獲得的收入；
•對本公司自有及租賃的不動產或投資價值產生負面影響；
